references.text: The women who accompanied Jesus from Galilee were previously described in [ref:Luk 8:2-3|Luke 8:2-3], where it mentions women such as Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Susanna, who served Jesus with their possessions and followed him.
[ref:Matt 27:55-56|Matthew 27:55-56] also mentions the women from Galilee who had followed Jesus and served him, and who were present at the crucifixion and burial.
[ref:Mark 15:40-41|Mark 15:40-41] is a parallel account describing the women who watched the crucifixion from a distance—women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him.
[ref:Mark 15:47|Mark 15:47] tells that Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, saw where Jesus was laid, which corresponds to the women in Luke observing the tomb and how the body was placed.
[ref:Matt 27:61|Matthew 27:61] describes how Mary Magdalene and the other Mary sat facing the tomb, confirming that the women carefully observed the burial site.

[ref:Luk 23:49|Luke 23:49] mentions earlier in the same chapter that the women who had followed Jesus from Galilee stood watching the crucifixion from a distance, and verse 55 adds that they also followed to the tomb.
[ref:Luk 24:1-3|Luke 24:1-3] is the direct continuation where these same women return to the tomb on the first day of the week with fragrant spices, but find the tomb empty.
[ref:Luk 23:56|Luke 23:56] is the immediate continuation where the women go home and prepare fragrant spices and ointments, and then observe the Sabbath rest according to the law.
[ref:Luk 24:10|Luke 24:10] finally identifies some of these women by name: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, as well as the other women who were with them.
